failures.test: POST /api/billing/webhook > returns 200 and upserts the mapped status for customer.subscription.updated
failures.failure_message: AssertionError: expected 500 to be 200. Route returns 500 because handleEvent throws TypeError: subscriptionsRepo.getSubscriptionByStripeId is not a function.
failures.hypothesis: The webhook route (per contract) calls subscriptionsRepo.getSubscriptionByStripeId(subscription.id) inside upsertFromStripeSubscription for customer.subscription.updated/deleted events. The test's subscriptionsRepoMock only defines upsertSubscription/isEventProcessed/markEventProcessed and omits getSubscriptionByStripeId, so calling it throws and the route returns 500 via its outer try/catch.
failures.fix_action: Add `getSubscriptionByStripeId: vi.fn()` to subscriptionsRepoMock and, in the two failing tests, do `subscriptionsRepoMock.getSubscriptionByStripeId.mockResolvedValue(null)` (or a stub row) before invoking POST so upsertFromStripeSubscription can proceed and pick up userId from subscription.metadata.userId.

failures.test: POST /api/billing/webhook > returns 200 and upserts a canceled subscription for customer.subscription.deleted
failures.failure_message: AssertionError: expected 500 to be 200. Same root cause as the updated-event failure: getSubscriptionByStripeId is undefined on the mock repo.
failures.hypothesis: Identical mock gap: getSubscriptionByStripeId is not stubbed, so the route throws inside upsertFromStripeSubscription and the outer try/catch converts it to a 500. The contract explicitly lists getSubscriptionByStripeId on SubscriptionsRepository, so the route is behaving as specified.
failures.fix_action: Same fix as the updated-event test: extend subscriptionsRepoMock with getSubscriptionByStripeId and mockResolvedValue(null) in each subscription.updated/deleted test case.

failures.failure_message: tsc reports many errors: 'Cannot redeclare block-scoped variable' for authMock/stripeMock/subscriptionsRepoMock/buildSubscription across billing test files; 'Duplicate identifier SubscriptionStatus' between src/lib/db/__tests__/subscriptions.test.ts and src/lib/__tests__/entitlements.test.ts; and 'Property createPortalSession/constructWebhookEvent/upsertSubscription/isEventProcessed/markEventProcessed does not exist on type { createCheckoutSession: Mock<Procedure>; }' in portal.test.ts and webhook.test.ts.
failures.hypothesis: All these tsc errors have a single root cause: the test files (checkout.test.ts, portal.test.ts, subscription.test.ts, webhook.test.ts, entitlements.test.ts, subscriptions.test.ts) have no top-level import or export statement. In TypeScript, a .ts file without imports/exports is a script, not a module, so its top-level `const stripeMock`/`authMock`/`subscriptionsRepoMock`/`buildSubscription` and its local `type SubscriptionStatus` all live in the shared global scope and collide across files. Because the collision merges declaration shapes, tsc then complains that other tests reference properties (createPortalSession, upsertSubscription, ...) that don't exist on the narrowest `stripeMock`/`subscriptionsRepoMock` shape (checkout.test.ts's, which is the shortest).
failures.fix_action: Turn each affected test file into a module. The cleanest fix is to add explicit imports at the top: `import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";` in every billing/entitlements/subscriptions test file (and to import `type { SubscriptionStatus, Subscription } from "@/lib/db/subscriptions.types"` in the two test files that currently redeclare them locally instead of the local `type` alias). Alternatively add `export {};` at the top of each file. That eliminates the global-scope collisions and the phantom 'property does not exist' cascade.

failures.test: npm scripts > npm run lint exits 0
failures.failure_message: next lint fails with '@next/next/no-assign-module-variable' at src/lib/__tests__/entitlements.test.ts:28:3 — 'const module = await import(ENTITLEMENTS_MODULE);'.
failures.hypothesis: The entitlements test assigns to a local variable named `module`, which Next.js's ESLint rule forbids because it collides with the CommonJS global `module`. The rule triggers even inside a function body. It's purely a lint-clean issue in the test file, not a code contract problem.
failures.fix_action: Rename the local `module` in src/lib/__tests__/entitlements.test.ts (line ~28) to something like `entitlementsModule` or destructure directly: `const { isUserPremium } = await import(ENTITLEMENTS_MODULE); return isUserPremium;`.

failures.test: npm scripts > npm run format:check exits 0
failures.failure_message: prettier --check reports 15 files with style issues: README.md, all four billing test files, checkout/portal/webhook route.ts, settings/page.tsx, entitlements.test.ts, auth/session.ts, db/subscriptions.ts, db/subscriptions.types.ts, entitlements.ts, stripe.ts.
failures.hypothesis: Multiple source files (route handlers, lib helpers, settings page) and multiple test files fail prettier formatting. Root cause is that the coder and tester wrote files without running `npm run format` before finishing. This spans both implementation (owner: coder) and tests (owner: tester), so at least one side needs to reformat every file it owns; simplest orchestration is to run `npm run format` once.
failures.fix_action: Run `npm run format` (or `npx prettier --write .`) to reformat all 15 flagged files. Verify with `npm run format:check`. Both coder- and tester-owned files are affected but a single sweep resolves them.

failures.failure_message: next build fails during 'Linting and checking validity of types' with the same @next/next/no-assign-module-variable error in src/lib/__tests__/entitlements.test.ts:28:3.
failures.hypothesis: Same root cause as the `npm run lint` failure: the test file's `const module = await import(...)` trips Next's lint rule, and `next build` runs lint as part of the build. Fixing the lint error fixes the build. There may still be secondary tsc issues surfaced by `next build`, but they share fate with the typescript.test.ts remediation above.
failures.fix_action: Same rename as the lint failure — replace the `module` identifier in entitlements.test.ts. After the tester fixes the module-name issue and the tsc/module-scope issues described in the typescript.test.ts failure, re-run `npm run build` to confirm it succeeds.
